1. ESTABLISHMENT ORDER

COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA
Consumer Affairs Portfolio

ESTABLISHMENT ORDER NO. 2019/14

I, the Minister for Consumer Affairs, pursuant to section 12 of the Consumer Product Safety Act 2011 (Cth), hereby establish the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (hereafter "the Committee") to provide independent expert advice on matters relating to the safety of consumer products supplied in Australia.

The Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee was established_date 2019-03-14. Record status: current.

This Order takes effect on the date of its execution.

Signed and sealed this fourteenth day of March 2019.

[SIGNATURE]

The Hon. Margaret Chen
Minister for Consumer Affairs

2. CHARTER OF THE COMMITTEE

2.1 Role and Functions

The Committee shall advise the Minister and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) on:

a) the identification and assessment of hazards associated with consumer products;
b) the development of safety standards and recall protocols;
c) priority areas for product safety research and data collection;
d) emerging risks arising from new technologies, import trends, or changes in consumer behaviour;
e) the effectiveness of existing regulatory measures and educational campaigns.

2.2 Status

The Committee is a non-statutory advisory body. It does not hold regulatory or enforcement powers. Recommendations are made to the Minister, who retains final authority over policy decisions.

2.3 Accountability

The Committee reports to the Minister through the Chair. The Committee shall table a report of its activities at least once each calendar year.

2.4 Term

The Committee shall continue in operation until such time as the Minister determines that its functions have been fulfilled or are otherwise no longer required.

---

3. MEMBERSHIP REGISTER

The Committee consists of a Chair, Deputy Chair, and not fewer than eight nor more than twelve additional members. Members are appointed by the Minister on the recommendation of the Chair or the relevant portfolio agency.

4. TERMS OF APPOINTMENT

**5. SUBCOMMITTEE STRUCTURE AND CHARTERS**

The Committee may establish subcommittees to examine specific matters within its terms of reference. Subcommittees report to the Committee and may not act independently of it except where expressly authorised by a resolution of the Committee.

Each subcommittee operates under a charter approved by the Committee. Charters set out the subcommittee's purpose, composition, reporting lines, and duration. A subcommittee ceases to exist when its charter is revoked, its task is completed, or its term expires, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

**5.1 Quality Assurance Subcommittee**

The Quality Assurance Subcommittee was established by resolution of the Committee at its meeting on 10 September 2019 (Resolution 2019/14). Its purpose is to advise the Committee on matters relating to the quality and reliability of consumer product safety data, testing methodologies, and compliance verification.

*Functions*

The Subcommittee's functions are to:

a) Review and recommend quality standards for product safety data submitted to the Committee by regulators, industry, and consumer organisations;

b) Examine testing laboratory accreditation and proficiency testing arrangements relevant to consumer products;

c) Advise on the design and conduct of surveys and studies commissioned by the Committee;

d) Identify data quality issues affecting the Committee's ability to assess product risks and recommend corrective actions;

e) Liaise with relevant technical experts and organisations, including Standards Australia and the National Association of Testing Authorities, as required; and

**Record of Amendments Adopted 2020–2023**

This section records amendments to the Charter of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (the Committee), established under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) and the Commission's Instrument of Establishment. Amendments are recorded in chronological order of adoption. Unless otherwise noted, each amendment took effect on the date of adoption.

---

**Amendment No. 1/2020 — Quorum Provisions**

Adopted: 18 June 2020 (Resolution RES-2020-002)

The Committee resolved to amend clause 7.2 of the Charter relating to quorum. The amendment was proposed by the Chair, seconded by Dr. James Park, and carried unanimously.

*Original text (clause 7.2):*

> A quorum shall be constituted by a simple majority of the members of the Committee.

*Amended text (clause 7.2):*

> A quorum shall be constituted by not less than five (5) members, provided that at least one member present is the Chair or Deputy Chair. Where the Chair and Deputy Chair are both absent, the meeting shall be adjourned and reconvened within fourteen (14) days.

Rationale recorded in the minutes of 18 June 2020: the previous quorum provision permitted meetings to proceed with a bare majority of four members, which the Committee considered insufficient for matters involving product safety recalls and mandatory standards. The amendment was circulated to the Minister for Consumer Affairs on 26 June 2020 and no objection was received within the statutory period.

---

**Amendment No. 2/2020 — Electronic Participation**

Adopted: 17 September 2020 (Resolution RES-2020-007)

In response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the associated travel restrictions, the Committee adopted an amendment to clause 7.4 to permit participation by electronic means.

*Original text (clause 7.4):*

> Members shall attend meetings in person unless excused by the Chair.

*Amended text (clause 7.4):*

> Members may attend meetings by video conference or other electronic means approved by the Chair. Members participating by electronic means shall be counted for the purposes of quorum and voting, provided that their identity and participation can be verified by the Secretary.

The amendment was adopted by majority vote, with Ms. Emily Chen abstaining. Ms. Chen noted that she had no objection to the substance of the amendment but considered that the verification requirement was operationally unclear. The Secretary was directed to develop guidance on verification methods, which was subsequently issued as Secretariat Guidance Note SG-2020-01 on 12 October 2020.

---

**Amendment No. 3/2021 — Term Limits for the Chair**

Adopted: 18 February 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-001)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 5.3 regarding the term of the Chair.

*Original text (clause 5.3):*

> The Chair shall be appointed by the Minister for a term not exceeding three (3) years and may be reappointed.

*Amended text (clause 5.3):*

> The Chair shall be appointed by the Minister for a term not exceeding three (3) years and may be reappointed for one further term not exceeding three (3) years. No member shall serve as Chair for more than six (6) years in total.

The amendment was proposed by Mr. Robert Hughes and seconded by Dr. Park. The Committee noted that the amendment aligned the Charter with the Commission's broader governance framework. The Minister was notified of the amendment on 25 February 2021; no objection was received.

---

**Amendment No. 4/2021 — Conflict of Interest Declaration**

Adopted: 20 May 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-004)

The Committee amended clause 9.1 to strengthen conflict of interest provisions following a review of the Committee's handling of a matter involving a member with a financial interest in a manufacturer under investigation.

*Original text (clause 9.1):*

> A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest and shall not participate in any decision on that matter.

**Amendment No. 5/2021 — Electronic Participation and Voting**

Adopted: 19 August 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-007)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 7.2 regarding electronic participation in meetings. The amendment formalised the practice that had been in place since March 2020 due to travel restrictions.

*Amended text (clause 7.2):*

> Members may participate in any meeting by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means approved by the Chair. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted for the purposes of quorum and voting, provided that their identity and participation can be verified by the Secretary in accordance with Secretariat Guidance Note SG-2020-01.

The amendment was moved by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Emily Chen. The Committee noted that the guidance note had been in operation for nearly a year and that verification procedures had worked well in practice. No objections were raised.

**Amendment No. 6/2021 — Deputy Chair**

Adopted: 18 November 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-011)

The Committee adopted an amendment to insert a new clause 5.4 regarding the appointment of a Deputy Chair.

*New text (clause 5.4):*

> The Committee shall elect from among its members a Deputy Chair who shall act as Chair in the absence of the Chair or when the Chair is unable to act. The Deputy Chair shall hold office for a term of two (2) years and may be re-elected.

The amendment was proposed by Ms. Chen and seconded by Mr. Hughes. In discussion, Mr. Hughes noted that the absence of a formal deputy arrangement had caused delays in the approval of two product recall notices in early 2021 when the Chair was unavailable. The Committee agreed that the Deputy Chair should not automatically succeed to the Chair in the event of a vacancy, and that the Minister would be consulted in such circumstances.

---

**Amendment No. 7/2022 — Quorum for Subcommittees**

Adopted: 17 February 2022 (Resolution RES-2022-002)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 8.4 regarding quorum for subcommittees.

*Original text (clause 8.4):*

> A subcommittee may meet and conduct business when at least three (3) members are present.

*Amended text (clause 8.4):*

> A subcommittee may meet and conduct business when at least half of its appointed members are present, provided that not less than three (3) members are present.

The amendment was moved by Mr. Hughes and seconded by Dr. Park. The change was prompted by the experience of the Product Safety Data Subcommittee, which had been unable to meet on three occasions in late 2021 because only two of its four members were available. The amendment was adopted unanimously.

**Amendment No. 8/2022 — Public Statements**

Adopted: 19 May 2022 (Resolution RES-2022-005)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 11.2 regarding public statements.

*Original text (clause 11.2):*

> The Chair may make public statements on behalf of the Committee.

*Amended text (clause 11.2):*

> The Chair may make public statements on behalf of the Committee. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair may make public statements on matters that have been the subject of a Committee decision. No other member shall make public statements purporting to represent the Committee unless authorised by the Chair.

The amendment was proposed by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Chen. The amendment was in response to an incident in March 2022 in which a member had commented to a journalist on a pending recall investigation, and the comments were reported as representing the Committee's view. The Committee noted that the member had not intended to misrepresent the Committee but that the Charter should be clear on this point.

The amendment was proposed by Ms. Chen and seconded by Mr. Hughes. **Amendment No. 10/2023 — Conflict of Interest**

Adopted: 15 June 2023 (Resolution RES-2023-004)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 9.2 regarding the declaration and management of conflicts of interest.

*Original text (clause 9.2):*

> A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest and shall not participate in the discussion or decision on that matter unless the Committee otherwise determines.

*Amended text (clause 9.2):*

> A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest at the earliest opportunity and shall not participate in the discussion or decision on that matter unless the Committee otherwise determines. The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes. Where the interest is financial, the member shall also refrain from attending any closed session relating to the matter.

The amendment was moved by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Chen. The change was prompted by a review of the Committee's procedures following a matter in early 2023 in which a member's interest was declared only after discussion had commenced. The Committee agreed that earlier declaration would assist in maintaining the integrity of its processes. The amendment was adopted by a vote of 6 in favour, 1 against, with 1 abstention.

**Amendment No. 11/2023 — Appointment of Deputy Chair**

Adopted: 21 September 2023 (Resolution RES-2023-007)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 5.3 regarding the appointment of the Deputy Chair.

*Original text (clause 5.3):*

*Amended text (clause 5.3):*

(b) to monitor and review the effectiveness of product safety measures;

Product Safety Standard PS-2020-02 (Children's folding cots – hinge and locking

From that date, certificates of compliance issued against PS-2020-02 will no longer be

relevant provisions of PS-2023-01.

A transitional arrangement applies. Goods that were already in the supply chain, or that
were manufactured before 2023-04-01 and can be traced to a certificate issued against
PS-2020-02, may continue to be supplied until 2023-09-30. After that date, all goods must

prioritise these applications to minimise disruption.

New standard – PS-2023-01

Product Safety Standard PS-2023-01 – Children's folding cots – hinge and locking
mechanisms (second edition)

Effective date: 2023-04-01.

This standard replaces PS-2020-02 in its entirety. It has been developed following a
review of incident data relating to folding cot hinge failures and unexpected collapse.
The review identified a small number of products in which the hinge locking mechanism
could be partially engaged and still allow the cot to be set up, creating a risk of
collapse during use.

Key changes from PS-2020-02 are:

- the hinge lock must now be automatically engaged when the cot is fully opened, and must
  not require a separate manual action by the carer;
- the force required to release a hinge lock has been increased, with a minimum release
  force of 45 N applied at the release point;
- a new test has been added for repeated opening and closing cycles, set at 2,000 cycles,
  with the cot inspected for hinge wear and lock function after every 500 cycles;
- the marking requirements now include a warning label stating "Always check that all
  hinge locks are engaged before placing a child in the cot" – the label must be affixed
  to the inside of the cot frame, near the hinge, and must be legible after 500 cleaning
  cycles using the standard cleaning agent specified in Appendix B of the standard.

The test methods in PS-2023-01 have been aligned with the current edition of AS/NZS 2172
where practicable, but the Office notes that AS/NZS 2172 does not yet include the
automatic engagement requirement. Suppliers should not assume that compliance with
AS/NZS 2172 alone is sufficient for compliance with PS-2023-01.

Compliance dates:

- For goods manufactured on or after 2023-04-01: full compliance required from the date
  of manufacture.
- For goods manufactured before 2023-04-01: the transitional arrangement described above
  applies until 2023-09-30.

The Office has prepared a guidance note (GN-2023-05, "Transition arrangements for
children's folding cots") which sets out the documentation required to support the
transitional arrangement. The guidance note is available on the Office website.

PS-2023-01. The correction applies to Section 5.2.3, paragraph (d).

The original text read: "Apply the release force in a horizontal direction, parallel to
the hinge axis."

1. ESTABLISHMENT ORDER

COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA
Consumer Affairs Portfolio

ESTABLISHMENT ORDER NO. 2019/14

I, the Minister for Consumer Affairs, pursuant to section 12 of the Consumer Product Safety Act 2011 (Cth), hereby establish the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (hereafter "the Committee") to provide independent expert advice on matters relating to the safety of consumer products supplied in Australia.

The Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee was established_date 2019-03-14. Record status: current.

This Order takes effect on the date of its execution.

Signed and sealed this fourteenth day of March 2019.

[SIGNATURE]

The Hon. Margaret Chen
Minister for Consumer Affairs

---

2. CHARTER OF THE COMMITTEE

2.1 Role and Functions

The Committee shall advise the Minister and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) on:

a) the identification and assessment of hazards associated with consumer products;
b) the development of safety standards and recall protocols;
c) priority areas for product safety research and data collection;
d) emerging risks arising from new technologies, import trends, or changes in consumer behaviour;
e) the effectiveness of existing regulatory measures and educational campaigns.

2.2 Status

The Committee is a non-statutory advisory body. It does not hold regulatory or enforcement powers. Recommendations are made to the Minister, who retains final authority over policy decisions.

2.3 Accountability

The Committee reports to the Minister through the Chair. The Committee shall table a report of its activities at least once each calendar year.

2.4 Term

The Committee shall continue in operation until such time as the Minister determines that its functions have been fulfilled or are otherwise no longer required.

---

3. MEMBERSHIP REGISTER

The Committee consists of a Chair, Deputy Chair, and not fewer than eight nor more than twelve additional members. Members are appointed by the Minister on the recommendation of the Chair or the relevant portfolio agency.

**5. SUBCOMMITTEE STRUCTURE AND CHARTERS**

The Committee may establish subcommittees to examine specific matters within its terms of reference. Subcommittees report to the Committee and may not act independently of it except where expressly authorised by a resolution of the Committee.

Each subcommittee operates under a charter approved by the Committee. Charters set out the subcommittee's purpose, composition, reporting lines, and duration. A subcommittee ceases to exist when its charter is revoked, its task is completed, or its term expires, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

**5.1 Quality Assurance Subcommittee**

The Quality Assurance Subcommittee was established by resolution of the Committee at its meeting on 10 September 2019 (Resolution 2019/14). Its purpose is to advise the Committee on matters relating to the quality and reliability of consumer product safety data, testing methodologies, and compliance verification.

*Charter*

|------|--------|
| Name | Quality Assurance Subcommittee |
| Parent body | Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee |
| Established | 10 September 2019 (Resolution 2019/14) |
| Reporting line | Reports directly to the Committee at each scheduled meeting; may also provide written advice between meetings |
| Term | Initial term of three years, expiring 30 September 2022, unless extended by the Committee |

| Quorum | Three members, of whom one must be the Subcommittee Chair or Deputy Chair |

The Quality Assurance Subcommittee has parent_body Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee. Record status: current. This relationship is current and remains in force as of the date of this Charter. No change to the reporting line has been proposed or approved since the subcommittee's establishment.

*Functions*

The Subcommittee's functions are to:

a) Review and recommend quality standards for product safety data submitted to the Committee by regulators, industry, and consumer organisations;

b) Examine testing laboratory accreditation and proficiency testing arrangements relevant to consumer products;

c) Advise on the design and conduct of surveys and studies commissioned by the Committee;

d) Identify data quality issues affecting the Committee's ability to assess product risks and recommend corrective actions;

e) Liaise with relevant technical experts and organisations, including Standards Australia and the National Association of Testing Authorities, as required; and

f) Report to the Committee on any matter referred to it by the Committee.

*Membership*

Membership of the Subcommittee is drawn from the Committee's own membership and from external experts co-opted with the approval of the Committee Chair.

**AMENDMENTS TO THE CHARTER AND GOVERNANCE RECORDS OF THE AUSTRALIAN CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY COMMITTEE**

**Record of Amendments Adopted 2020–2023**

This section records amendments to the Charter of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (the Committee), established under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) and the Commission's Instrument of Establishment. Amendments are recorded in chronological order of adoption. Unless otherwise noted, each amendment took effect on the date of adoption.

---

**Amendment No. 1/2020 — Quorum Provisions**

Adopted: 18 June 2020 (Resolution RES-2020-002)

The Committee resolved to amend clause 7.2 of the Charter relating to quorum. The amendment was proposed by the Chair, seconded by Dr. James Park, and carried unanimously.

*Original text (clause 7.2):*

> A quorum shall be constituted by a simple majority of the members of the Committee.

*Amended text (clause 7.2):*

> A quorum shall be constituted by not less than five (5) members, provided that at least one member present is the Chair or Deputy Chair. Where the Chair and Deputy Chair are both absent, the meeting shall be adjourned and reconvened within fourteen (14) days.

Rationale recorded in the minutes of 18 June 2020: the previous quorum provision permitted meetings to proceed with a bare majority of four members, which the Committee considered insufficient for matters involving product safety recalls and mandatory standards. The amendment was circulated to the Minister for Consumer Affairs on 26 June 2020 and no objection was received within the statutory period.

---

**Amendment No. 2/2020 — Electronic Participation**

Adopted: 17 September 2020 (Resolution RES-2020-007)

In response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the associated travel restrictions, the Committee adopted an amendment to clause 7.4 to permit participation by electronic means.

*Original text (clause 7.4):*

> Members shall attend meetings in person unless excused by the Chair.

*Amended text (clause 7.4):*

> Members may attend meetings by video conference or other electronic means approved by the Chair. Members participating by electronic means shall be counted for the purposes of quorum and voting, provided that their identity and participation can be verified by the Secretary.

The amendment was adopted by majority vote, with Ms. Emily Chen abstaining. Ms. Chen noted that she had no objection to the substance of the amendment but considered that the verification requirement was operationally unclear. The Secretary was directed to develop guidance on verification methods, which was subsequently issued as Secretariat Guidance Note SG-2020-01 on 12 October 2020.

---

**Amendment No. 3/2021 — Term Limits for the Chair**

Adopted: 18 February 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-001)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 5.3 regarding the term of the Chair.

*Original text (clause 5.3):*

> The Chair shall be appointed by the Minister for a term not exceeding three (3) years and may be reappointed.

*Amended text (clause 5.3):*

> The Chair shall be appointed by the Minister for a term not exceeding three (3) years and may be reappointed for one further term not exceeding three (3) years. No member shall serve as Chair for more than six (6) years in total.

The amendment was proposed by Mr. Robert Hughes and seconded by Dr. Park. The Committee noted that the amendment aligned the Charter with the Commission's broader governance framework. The Minister was notified of the amendment on 25 February 2021; no objection was received.

---

**Amendment No. 4/2021 — Conflict of Interest Declaration**

Adopted: 20 May 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-004)

The Committee amended clause 9.1 to strengthen conflict of interest provisions following a review of the Committee's handling of a matter involving a member with a financial interest in a manufacturer under investigation.

*Original text (clause 9.1):*

> A member who has a conflict of interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest and shall not participate in any decision on that matter.

**Charter and Governance Records of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee**

---

**Amendment No. 5/2021 — Electronic Participation and Voting**

Adopted: 19 August 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-007)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 7.2 regarding electronic participation in meetings. The amendment formalised the practice that had been in place since March 2020 due to travel restrictions.

*Amended text (clause 7.2):*

> Members may participate in any meeting by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means approved by the Chair. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted for the purposes of quorum and voting, provided that their identity and participation can be verified by the Secretary in accordance with Secretariat Guidance Note SG-2020-01.

The amendment was moved by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Emily Chen. The Committee noted that the guidance note had been in operation for nearly a year and that verification procedures had worked well in practice. No objections were raised.

---

**Amendment No. 6/2021 — Deputy Chair**

Adopted: 18 November 2021 (Resolution RES-2021-011)

The Committee adopted an amendment to insert a new clause 5.4 regarding the appointment of a Deputy Chair.

*New text (clause 5.4):*

> The Committee shall elect from among its members a Deputy Chair who shall act as Chair in the absence of the Chair or when the Chair is unable to act. The Deputy Chair shall hold office for a term of two (2) years and may be re-elected.

The amendment was proposed by Ms. Chen and seconded by Mr. Hughes. In discussion, Mr. Hughes noted that the absence of a formal deputy arrangement had caused delays in the approval of two product recall notices in early 2021 when the Chair was unavailable. The Committee agreed that the Deputy Chair should not automatically succeed to the Chair in the event of a vacancy, and that the Minister would be consulted in such circumstances.

---

**Amendment No. 7/2022 — Quorum for Subcommittees**

Adopted: 17 February 2022 (Resolution RES-2022-002)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 8.4 regarding quorum for subcommittees.

*Original text (clause 8.4):*

> A subcommittee may meet and conduct business when at least three (3) members are present.

*Amended text (clause 8.4):*

> A subcommittee may meet and conduct business when at least half of its appointed members are present, provided that not less than three (3) members are present.

The amendment was moved by Mr. Hughes and seconded by Dr. Park. The change was prompted by the experience of the Product Safety Data Subcommittee, which had been unable to meet on three occasions in late 2021 because only two of its four members were available. The amendment was adopted unanimously.

---

**Amendment No. 8/2022 — Public Statements**

Adopted: 19 May 2022 (Resolution RES-2022-005)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 11.2 regarding public statements.

*Original text (clause 11.2):*

> The Chair may make public statements on behalf of the Committee.

*Amended text (clause 11.2):*

> The Chair may make public statements on behalf of the Committee. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair may make public statements on matters that have been the subject of a Committee decision. No other member shall make public statements purporting to represent the Committee unless authorised by the Chair.

The amendment was proposed by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Chen. The amendment was in response to an incident in March 2022 in which a member had commented to a journalist on a pending recall investigation, and the comments were reported as representing the Committee's view. The Committee noted that the member had not intended to misrepresent the Committee but that the Charter should be clear on this point.

---

**Amendment No. 9/2023 — Annual Reporting**

Adopted: 16 February 2023 (Resolution RES-2023-001)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 12.1 regarding annual reporting.

*Original text (clause 12.1):*

**Amendment No. 9/2023 — Annual Reporting (continued)**

*Amended text (clause 12.1):*

> The Committee shall prepare and publish an annual report on its activities, including a summary of matters considered, recommendations made, and the status of implementation of such recommendations. The report shall be submitted to the Minister within three months of the end of each financial year and shall be made publicly available on the Committee's website.

The amendment was proposed by Ms. Chen and seconded by Mr. Hughes. The revision was intended to align the Committee's reporting obligations with the transparency expectations set out in the *Consumer Product Safety Act* and to provide a consistent public record of the Committee's work. The amendment was adopted unanimously.

---

**Amendment No. 10/2023 — Conflict of Interest**

Adopted: 15 June 2023 (Resolution RES-2023-004)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 9.2 regarding the declaration and management of conflicts of interest.

*Original text (clause 9.2):*

> A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest and shall not participate in the discussion or decision on that matter unless the Committee otherwise determines.

*Amended text (clause 9.2):*

> A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee shall declare that interest at the earliest opportunity and shall not participate in the discussion or decision on that matter unless the Committee otherwise determines. The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes. Where the interest is financial, the member shall also refrain from attending any closed session relating to the matter.

The amendment was moved by Dr. Park and seconded by Ms. Chen. The change was prompted by a review of the Committee's procedures following a matter in early 2023 in which a member's interest was declared only after discussion had commenced. The Committee agreed that earlier declaration would assist in maintaining the integrity of its processes. The amendment was adopted by a vote of 6 in favour, 1 against, with 1 abstention.

---

**Amendment No. 11/2023 — Appointment of Deputy Chair**

Adopted: 21 September 2023 (Resolution RES-2023-007)

The Committee adopted an amendment to clause 5.3 regarding the appointment of the Deputy Chair.

*Original text (clause 5.3):*

> The Committee shall appoint one of its members as Deputy Chair, who shall act in the Chair's absence.

*Amended text (clause 5.3):*

> The Committee shall appoint one of its members as Deputy Chair, who shall act in the Chair's absence. The Deputy Chair shall be appointed for a term of two years and may be reappointed. If the office of Deputy Chair becomes vacant, the Committee shall appoint a replacement at its next meeting.

The amendment was proposed by Mr. Hughes and seconded by Dr. Park. The change was intended to provide greater certainty regarding the tenure of the Deputy Chair and to ensure that the position could be filled promptly if vacated. The amendment was adopted unanimously.

---

**Consolidated Charter — Current Version (as at 1 July 2024)**

The following is the consolidated text of the Committee's Charter, incorporating all amendments adopted to date. This version supersedes all previous versions.

**1. Establishment**

1.1 The Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (the Committee) is established under section 32 of the *Consumer Product Safety Act* (the Act).

1.2 The Committee is an advisory body and does not have regulatory or enforcement powers.

**2. Objects**

2.1 The objects of the Committee are:

(a) to provide advice to the Minister on matters relating to consumer product safety;

(b) to monitor and review the effectiveness of product safety measures;

(c) to facilitate consultation between the Commonwealth, States and Territories, and other stakeholders;

(d) to identify emerging product safety issues and recommend appropriate responses.

Product Safety Standard PS-2020-02 (Children's folding cots – hinge and locking

Manufacturers holding a current certificate against PS-2020-02 should contact the Office
to arrange re-testing and re-certification against the new standard. The Office will
prioritise these applications to minimise disruption.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

New standard – PS-2023-01

Product Safety Standard PS-2023-01 – Children's folding cots – hinge and locking
mechanisms (second edition)

Effective date: 2023-04-01.

This standard replaces PS-2020-02 in its entirety. It has been developed following a
review of incident data relating to folding cot hinge failures and unexpected collapse.
The review identified a small number of products in which the hinge locking mechanism
could be partially engaged and still allow the cot to be set up, creating a risk of
collapse during use.

Key changes from PS-2020-02 are:

- the hinge lock must now be automatically engaged when the cot is fully opened, and must
  not require a separate manual action by the carer;
- the force required to release a hinge lock has been increased, with a minimum release
  force of 45 N applied at the release point;
- a new test has been added for repeated opening and closing cycles, set at 2,000 cycles,
  with the cot inspected for hinge wear and lock function after every 500 cycles;
- the marking requirements now include a warning label stating "Always check that all
  hinge locks are engaged before placing a child in the cot" – the label must be affixed
  to the inside of the cot frame, near the hinge, and must be legible after 500 cleaning
  cycles using the standard cleaning agent specified in Appendix B of the standard.

The test methods in PS-2023-01 have been aligned with the current edition of AS/NZS 2172
where practicable, but the Office notes that AS/NZS 2172 does not yet include the
automatic engagement requirement. Suppliers should not assume that compliance with
AS/NZS 2172 alone is sufficient for compliance with PS-2023-01.

Compliance dates:

- For goods manufactured on or after 2023-04-01: full compliance required from the date
  of manufacture.
- For goods manufactured before 2023-04-01: the transitional arrangement described above
  applies until 2023-09-30.

The Office has prepared a guidance note (GN-2023-05, "Transition arrangements for
children's folding cots") which sets out the documentation required to support the
transitional arrangement. The guidance note is available on the Office website.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Correction notice – PS-2023-01

The Office has issued a correction to the test procedure for hinge lock release force in
PS-2023-01. The correction applies to Section 5.2.3, paragraph (d).

The original text read: "Apply the release force in a horizontal direction, parallel to
the hinge axis."

REGULATORY STANDARD REGISTER OF THE OFFICE OF PRODUCT COMPLIANCE

Register of safety standards, mandatory standards, and bans administered by the Office, with
revision history and current status.

Maintained by: Standards & Compliance Unit
Last updated: 2024-11-18
Next scheduled review: 2025-03 (quarterly)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. REGISTER SUMMARY
------------------------------------------------------------------------

The register lists all product safety standards and bans currently in force, together with
standards that have been superseded or revoked during the period 2019 to date. Entries are
arranged by standard number. The status column indicates whether the entry is CURRENT,
SUPERSEDED, REVOKED, or UNDER REVIEW. Effective dates are shown in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).

Standards are reviewed on a rolling cycle. The review schedule for the next 12 months is set
out in Section 6. A full revision history for each standard is included in the individual
entries in Sections 2 to 5.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. MANDATORY STANDARDS – CURRENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------

PS-2019-03 – Child restraints for motor vehicles
Status: CURRENT (second edition)
First issued: 2019-06-30
Current edition effective: 2022-02-01
Next review due: 2025-06

Revision history:
- 2019-06-30: First edition issued. Included requirements for harness adjustment and
  side-impact protection.
- 2021-08-12: Draft second edition released for public comment. Comment period closed
  2021-10-08.
- 2022-01-14: Second edition published.
- 2022-02-01: Second edition came into effect. The first edition was withdrawn on this
  date. Goods certified against the first edition could continue to be supplied until
  2022-07-31, after which all supply required compliance with the second edition.

PS-2020-02 – Baby walkers
Status: CURRENT
First issued: 2020-03-15
Effective date: 2020-09-01
Last reviewed: 2023-05 (no changes required)

Revision history:
- 2020-03-15: Standard published.
- 2020-09-01: Standard came into effect. No transitional period applied.
- 2023-05-17: Five-year review completed. The review found no need for amendment. The
  standard remains in force unchanged.

PS-2021-04 – Household cots (non-folding)
Status: CURRENT
First issued: 2021-04-01
Effective date: 2021-10-01
Last reviewed: 2024-02 (minor amendments made)

Revision history:
- 2021-04-01: Standard published.
- 2021-10-01: Standard came into effect.
- 2024-02-09: Amendment 1 issued. The amendment clarified the test method for drop-side
  mechanisms and updated the labelling requirements. Amendment 1 came into effect on
  2024-08-01. Goods manufactured before 2024-08-01 could comply with either the original
  text or the amended text until 2025-01-31.

PS-2023-01 – Children's folding cots
Status: CURRENT
First issued: 2023-01-20
Effective date: 2023-04-01
Last reviewed: 2024-07 (correction issued, see below)

Revision history:
- 2023-01-20: Standard published.
- 2023-04-01: Standard came into effect, with a transitional arrangement for goods
  manufactured before that date (see guidance note GN-2023-05).
- 2023-08-30: Correction notice issued for Section 5.2.3, paragraph (d). The correction
  changed the direction of the applied release force from horizontal to vertical. The
  corrected text reads: "Apply the release force in a vertical direction, perpendicular
  to the hinge axis." The correction applies from the date of the notice; no compliance
  extension was granted.
- 2024-07-15: The Office confirmed that no further amendments are planned at this stage.
  The standard remains under routine review.
